Motivation and cool opportunities JUMP INTO HOW THE INTERDISCPLINARY ASPECTS ::: # Focused Design Constraints :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} # - # Size Regulation ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} # Front and back suspension All hydraulic brakes Firewall between driver and engine Proper electrical harnessing # Safety Regulation ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} # Performance Regulation # Turning Radius of Passing __ degree brake test ::: :::: ::: {.notes} JC-> Design constraints listed in our proposal and things we are most concerned by ::: # Prior Vehicles and Past Troubles :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew4.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew5.jpg) _2018 Front Suspension_ ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew6.png) 2015 Competition Team ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew7.png) 2012 \- Original Chassis Construction ::: :::: ::: {.notes} BH -> i’ll add pics if needed (by sunday/monday) ::: # Motivations for an Overhaul ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew8.jpg) | Outdated Chassis Model | Current chassis was made in ‘13
No aerodynamic considerations
New size requirements | | :-: | :-: | | Hydraulic Brakes | Hydraulic disk-pad brakes are standardized and required | | Outdated Materials | Aluminum chassis adds unnecessary weight and is restricting performance | | New front and rear suspension | Front suspension is hefty and complicates steering
No rear suspension system | | Steering and Driver Safety Systems | Steering columns need to be redesigned for turning radius requirements
Safety electronics need an update | | Fuel Cell Woes | Current FC is inconsistent and needs to be assessed for further use | ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew9.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew10.jpg) ::: {.notes} BH-> Ben will probably mention a bunch of stuff concerning the problems with the old car -> this is to connect the new design constraints, the trends for redesigns of the vehicles, and parts of the old car that needed to be rebuilt -> ALSO ADD Motivations for learning how to design a vehicle, 3D printing + machining, how to design for energy efficiency -> where the world is going sustainability wise ::: # 01 # Main Goals: How do we get more efficient? ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew11.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew12.jpg) _Work cut out for us?_ ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew13.png) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew14.png) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew15.png) ::: {.notes} -> speaking JC ::: # Fuel Cell Renewal & Feasibility Assessment :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} # Current FC woes # H2 gas moves along a membrane where it merges with O2 gas to make water and electricity An electric motor powers the vehicle -> 0 emission kinematic propulsion! # FC was bought in ‘19 and has had multiple start-up issues Possible need for FC rehydration & system renewals No benchmarking of potential power # How does a HFCV work? ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew16.jpg) ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew17.png) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew18.png) ::: :::: ::: {.notes} JC [how a hydrogen fuel cell works + necessary checks/troubleshooting with the fuel cell engine works] TALK MORE ABT THE SUSTAINABILITY ASPECTS AND ELECTRONICS ::: # Fuel Efficiency is King! # Shell Eco-Marathon measures the amount of hydrogen used to drive 3.9kms in less than 35 mins. # Weight kills efficiency # Our fuel efficiency model estimates ~3-4 MPGe gained per pound reduced. # 240+ MPG Gained # A potential >20% fuel efficiency increase by swapping to lighter material! ::: {.notes} JC [how fuel efficiency is calculated for the competition and how the model works + future plans for complications if needed] -> would be a good place to link the fuel efficiency calculations to the material changes/joint change [maybe next slide in next iteration] ::: # Suspension # CF Tube Δ # Material Impacts :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew19.png) ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} _Overall Weight \(Including Driver\):_ __ __ _243 ➔ 166 lbs \(31% Decrease\)_ _Fuel Efficiency:_ __ __ _1288➔ 1598MPGe \(24% Increase\)_ _Overall Weight:_ __ __ _25 ➔ ~12 lbs \(With Added Back\)_ ::: :::: ::: {.notes} BH ::: # 2: # New Chassis & Materials Research ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew20.png) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew21.png) ::: {.notes} BH - Insert SAP model ::: # Connection Methods: Carbon Fiber Tubes :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} # Benefits: Reliable material strength Machining Constraints Drawbacks: Heavier Welding is difficult Potential Additional Strength: Cable/String through rod # Aluminum Inserts ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew22.png) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew23.png) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew24.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew25.jpg) ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} # 3D Printed Collars # Benefits: Lightweight and strong Flexible in design Drawbacks: Layer Shear Failure Misprints Potential Additional Strength: Screw Connections ::: :::: ::: {.notes} BH ::: # Tension Tests :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew26.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew27.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew28.png) ::: :::: ::: {.notes} BH - 2 versions of carbon fiber - similar results with just epoxy. More confidence in the wrapped CF with how it is made. Approximately 400 lbs to rip out metal insert, initially 100-200 for plastic -> at least 400 lbs with hardware. Sloppy weld ::: # Tension Test Results + Cost Analysis _Maximum Simulated Loads \(200 lb Driver\): 300 lbs \(T\) & 540 lbs _ _\(C\)_ _Design Goals: 1000 lbs \(T\) & 2000 lbs _ _\(C\)_ | | SW (.5” D) | LW (.75” D) | Average (Wrapped) | | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | | Maximum (lbs) | 561.1629 | 596.35785 | 578.760375 | | Modulus (lbs/in) | 9425 | 9297.626316 | 9361.313158 | | Est. Displacement before Fail | 0.05 | 0.055 | 0.055 | ::: {.notes} TALK ABOUT WHAT WE THINK THIS MEANS FOR MATERIALS CHOICES (what we’d recommend) + what future tests may reveal Test results -> BH , Cost stuff -> BH ::: # Failures so far :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew29.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew30.jpg) ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew31.jpg) ![](img%5CE90%20Mid-Semester%20Reivew32.jpg) ::: :::: ::: {.notes} JC -> pictures of failed prints, failures from the fuel cell troubleshoots, testing moments ::: # Timeline and Next Steps :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="33%"} _Conduct joint compression test/ 2nd round of material iterations_ ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} _CAD design for back and front suspension of current vehicle_ _Fabricate suspensions from Chrome Moly tube_ _Installation \+ _ _Adjustments_ _ to Previous Vehicle_ _Practice Presentations \+ Final Report_ ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} _Final Joinery Designs_ ::: :::: ::: {.notes} BH ::: # Thanks! # Do you have any questions? _Please keep this slide for attribution_
